title: Continuity codex: night relay and action rollup 2029-01-09
shift_summary: Night relay: 23:00–07:00 PST. Primary focus was addressing a sudden P95/P99 latency regression for hosted text-generation routes, and validating the temporary mitigation. Teams involved: runtime batcher, autoscaler, routing. No customer-facing outages persisted past 01:20 PST; intermittent higher tail latency observed through 03:00 PST. Overall customer impact: elevated tail latency (4–12% of requests above SLO) for 90m window. Cost impact: estimated additional GPU-hours during remediation window.
notable_incidents: Incident A — tail latency spike (23:42–01:20 PST): P99 for /v1/generate-gpt-large-3 increased from ~450ms to ~1.2s. Symptom: large request queues in batcher pod logs and per-token stall traces. Initial alert triggered by p99-latency > 1s for 5m.

Incident B — routing mismatch causing 502 errors (00:05–00:30 PST): Requests intended for `gpt-large-3-quant` were routed to an incompatible variant due to a stale routing policy cache on the control plane node; error rate peaked at 0.8% on affected routes and auto-retries amplified load briefly.
actions_taken: 01:00 PST: Rolled back batcher config change deployed at 22:50 (reverted max-batch-size bump and added target-latency cap). Patch ID: runtime PR#4587
00:20 PST: Temporarily increased batcher replica count: kubectl scale deployment/batcher -n inference --replicas=10
00:40 PST: Forced control-plane routing cache flush on two coordinator nodes (systemctl restart redwood-routing.service) to clear stale policy; confirmed via routing-snapshot check
01:30 PST: Enabled conservative autoscaler override for hosting pool — min-replicas increased to avoid aggressive scale-in windows until full root cause remediation
02:10 PST: Enabled per-route fallback to smaller-model-variant for latency-sensitive routes as a precautionary policy change

runbook_deltas: Batcher playbook: introduce 'queue-depth to scale' heuristic and clear instructions for replica scaling vs config rollback
Routing playbook: explicit cache-flush step and verification queries after control-plane deploys
Oncall checklist: include timeout budget for configuration rollbacks (how long to monitor before marking as mitigated)
metrics_snapshot: At 23:30 PST baseline P95=520ms, P99=480ms. At peak window (23:50–00:30) P95=930ms, P99=1.2s. Error rate for /v1/generate rose from 0.05% to 0.8% during routing mismatch. Batcher queue depth increased from median 8 to sustained 52 across pods.
commands_ran: kubectl -n inference logs deployment/batcher --since=2h --tail=200 | grep queue_depth
ssh coordinator-02 'systemctl restart redwood-routing.service && journalctl -u redwood-routing -n 200'
investigation_notes: Traces show long waits in attention-kernel stage but latency correlated with batcher queue depth rather than GPU saturation. Per-GPU metrics (SM utilization) remained ~60–70% — not fully saturated.

Recent config change (22:50 deploy) increased max-batch-size from 48 to 96 without commensurate target-latency cap. Under typical load this improved throughput, but with bursty short requests it increased per-request tail due to head-of-line blocking.

Autoscaler had a scale-in event at 23:20 that reduced batcher replicas from 12 to 6 during early window; combined with larger batch size this produced visible queue buildup. Autoscaler logs show the decision was based on CPU utilization thresholds; metric selection needs review.

Routing policy cache TTL default of 5m applied; one coordinator node failed to pull the updated policy during deploy (transient API timeout). This left a subset of requests routed to legacy variant until cache expired or manual flush applied.
risk_assessment: Medium-high: root cause is a combination of config regression + autoscaler tuning that can recur on future config changes. Short-term mitigations reduce immediate recurrence risk; long-term changes required in testing and autoscaler heuristics. Customer-facing SLO breaches were modest in duration but tail-latency sensitivity could impact some latency-critical customers.

Monitor p99 and batcher queue depth dashboards; if p99>900ms AND avg queue depth>30, escalate to runtime-oncall immediately
Run control-plane cache-flush and confirm with routing-snapshot endpoint after any policy deploys
